initial_plan.can_answer: partly: the data can show the annual count of Brooklyn crashes with at least one pedestrian injured or killed, but cannot establish an exposure-adjusted change in road safety or explain causes
initial_plan.metric: annual number of Brooklyn crashes with one or more pedestrians injured or killed
initial_plan.denominator: one police-reported crash row per crash; the metric is a count, not a rate
initial_plan.population: all police-reported motor vehicle crashes in Brooklyn in each included calendar year; count a crash once if its recorded pedestrian injury or fatality count is positive
initial_plan.years: 2013 through the latest complete calendar year present in the file

facts: The file has dated records from 2013-01-01 through 2026-06-11; 2026 is partial, so the final comparison uses 2013-2025.
The file stores borough labels in uppercase; matching after trimming whitespace and ignoring case yields the Brooklyn population.
Among 2,132,218 dated NYC crash rows in 2013-2025, 659,713 (30.9%) have borough missing or unknown and cannot be assigned to Brooklyn; exclude and disclose them.

Within the selected Brooklyn rows in 2013-2025, the pedestrian injury and fatality fields have no missing or negative values. Zero is a valid recorded count, not an unknown/default to discard; keep those rows and count zero as zero.
No crash-date missingness occurs within the selected dated population.
decisions: Exclude rows with missing/unknown borough because they cannot be reliably assigned; disclose the excluded volume.
Retain valid zeros and all selected Brooklyn crash rows.

final_plan.can_answer: partly: shows the number of Brooklyn crashes with pedestrian injury or death, but not pedestrian exposure or risk and cannot establish whether overall road safety got better
final_plan.metric: annual number of distinct Brooklyn crash rows with one or more pedestrians injured or killed
final_plan.denominator: none; count each qualifying Brooklyn crash row once, regardless of the number of pedestrians injured or killed
final_plan.population: all police-reported motor vehicle crashes assigned to Brooklyn, 2013-2025; the metric counts the subset with at least one pedestrian injury or death
filters: pedestrian injury count > 0 or pedestrian fatality count > 0 for the event count
final_plan.limitations: Counts describe police-reported crashes with recorded pedestrian harm, not exposure-adjusted risk; 659,713 of 2,132,218 dated NYC crashes in 2013-2025 (30.9%) lack a usable borough and are excluded, and 2026 is partial and excluded.
